figures.finding: Zimbabwe has no child-performer permit: no employer may employ anyone under sixteen in any occupation (an apprentice under thirteen), save school or vocational work from thirteen, and no one under eighteen in work likely to jeopardise health, safety or morals; the Act names no exception for performing, so a paid child performer under sixteen falls under the bar (reading), as would a young writer or director employed.

value.under18: no work likely to jeopardise health, safety or morals

figures.applies: Labour Act [Chapter 28:01] s. 11, Veritas consolidated text.

sources.said: (1) Subject to subsection (3), no employer shall employ any person in any occupation— (a) as an apprentice who is under the age of thirteen years; (b) otherwise than as an apprentice who is under the age of sixteen years. ... (4) No employer shall cause any person under the age of eighteen years to perform any work which is likely to jeopardise that person’s health, safety or morals

figures.finding: A contract of employment made with a person under sixteen (or an apprenticeship under thirteen) is void and unenforceable against him, whether or not his guardian assisted him or he was married or emancipated, though he may enforce rights already accrued; an apprenticeship under eighteen made without the guardian's assistance is void too. No set-aside of earnings was found.

binding.under16: void (s. 11(2)); accrued rights enforceable by the minor

figures.applies: Labour Act s. 11(2), Veritas consolidated text.

sources.said: (2) Any contract of employment entered into in contravention of subsection (1), and any contract of apprenticeship with an apprentice below the age of eighteen years which was entered without the assistance of the apprentice’s guardian, shall be void and unenforceable against the person purportedly employed under such contract, whether or not (in the case of a contravention of paragraph (b) of subsection (1)) such person was assisted by his guardian, or was married or otherwise tacitly or expressly emancipated, but such person may enforce any rights that have accrued to him by or under such contract.

figures.finding: A minor may not be appointed a director of a Zimbabwean public company; for a private company the Act doesn't bar it but requires the secretary or principal shareholder to file a public statement with the Registrar when a director is affected by a disqualification that would apply in a public company (so a minor may direct a private company, disclosed: reading).
figures.applies: Companies and Other Business Entities Act [Chapter 24:31] s. 200, Veritas text.

sources.said: (1) Any of the following persons shall be disqualified from being appointed a director of a public company— (a) a body corporate; or (b) a minor or any other person under legal disability; ... (5) In relation to private companies, the secretary or principal shareholder shall file with the Registrar (within thirty days of becoming so aware) a statement in the event that a director of his or her company is or becomes affected by any of the disqualifications in this section that would apply to him or her if the director was the director of a public company
